lens: all three in turn: learning-scientist, examiner, learner-advocate (final score = mean of the three passes)

gates.G3_broken_graph: pass (walked S1.gate to END by reading every node: every next resolves to a node and every node has a way forward; validate was not run because this judge has no shell)
gates.G4_buttons_only: pass (every learner turn is a tap on a pre-written choice; no typing; no run-time model)

rationale.R1: Almost every new idea opens with a probe: S1.gate, S1.tissue, S1.vig, S2.entry, S2.brca_q, S2.male_q, S3.nipple, S3.skin, S4.t_pair, S4.t_n, S5.r1, S6.ls_p1, S6.ts_p1, S7.p1 to S7.p14. Exceptions tell first: S2.contrast, S3.mri, S4.t_prog, S6.ls_w1 and S6.ls_w2 (worked case), S6.ls_show.
rationale.R2: Strong trap work. Each of the 20 traps in the trap map appears in the walk, most in two or more forms (for example TR12 at S2.peau_q, S2.pred_q, S3.skin, S4.t_pair, S7.p8; TR27 at S5.r3, S5.t3_why, S8.axil). Tempting-then-refute feedback names the lure on most trap nodes (S2.entry_t10, S4.t_n_both, S5.t2_t14, S6.why_t16, S7.p9_t). Flaws: PTEN and STK11 are filler partials at S2.numbers_q (S2.numbers_pten, S2.numbers_stk); S8.male key 'Klinefelter' is the only non-gene option; S8.tam and S8.axil keys are the only long, rationale-bearing options; several wrong-option feedbacks (S4.t_which_skin, S4.t_n_neither, S4.t_img_neither) name no wrong model.
rationale.R3: All 12 objectives are probed on the main spine: O1 at S1.gate and S7.p1; O2 at S2.brca_q and S7.p5; O3 at S1.tissue, S1.vig, S3.imaging and S8.tis; O4 at S3.staging and S8.bone; O5 at S3.nipple and S4.t_pair; O6 at S4.t_n and S7.p7; O7 at S5.r1 and S7.p10; O8 at S5.r2 and S5.r3; O9 at S6.ls_p1 and S6.im_a; O10 at S6.ts_p1 and S7.p14; O11 at S6.tr_p1 and S7.p11; O12 at S5.r4 and S8.numb. Fast lanes (S2.entry_ok skip, S6.ls_p1_ok skip) still reach each objective.
rationale.R4: Most nodes are one idea and one question. Several stack ideas: S5.r2_e (four rules in one explanation), S5.r4_ok (nerve, winging and a summary), S6.ls_w2 (three steps). The generic opener 'That choice is not right.' appears on roughly 80 wrong-option nodes and is the main load and clarity problem. Terms are mostly plain; 'T4d', 'SLNB', 'ALND' are used without a gloss on first contact at S4.t_pair and S5.r3.
rationale.R5: Real adaptivity: hints on most early probes (S1.gate_hint, S1.tissue_hint, S2.entry_hint, S3.nipple_hint), 'Show me why' reveals, and a second explanation in another form on the key traps (S5.t2_size for TR14, S5.t3_why for TR27, S5.t4_nerve for TR15, S7 for most traps). Skip lanes exist at S2.entry_ok and S6.ls_p1_ok. Weak: the hint ladder is one level with no escalation; the 'Show me' explanations repeat verbatim on a second visit (S6.ls_show2, S6.ts_show2, S6.tt_show2 duplicate their first versions); S8.axil, S8.numb, S8.tam, S8.labc, S8.male and S5.t1_op offer no hint option.
rationale.R6: High-yield PYQ traps are drilled in exam form: 'which is NOT part of' (S7.p14, S7.p11, S7.p5), 'most common cause' versus 'cause to exclude' (S3.nipple, S7.p3), 'which statement is correct' on the Halsted/MRM and tamoxifen/raloxifene contrasts (S7.p10, S6.tt_p2). Old keys are named and their content is stated at first contact (S1.gate_reveal, S1.tissue_reveal, S2.numbers_ok). Lost points: S8.male and S8.tam are answerable by form, which an examiner would spot.
rationale.R7: Decisions are framed as clinical moments: the 45-year-old with an operable lump (S5.r1), the 42-year-old with a 2 cm cancer (S8.axil), the 36-year-old premenopausal woman (S6.ts_p2), the day-by-day stage III patient (S6.ls_p1), the bloody discharge at 35 (S3.nipple). The S7 run is mostly abstract 'which statement is correct' recognition, which costs points.
rationale.R8: Warm enough and addresses the learner directly, with no ability praise. Flat through repetition: 'That choice is not right.' opens almost every wrong-option feedback, and 'You were sure, so...' opens most sure notes. The S7 run in particular reads as one template repeated fourteen times.
rationale.R9: Most probes separate one wrong model from the right one, and the trap-mapped distractors make the path say a good deal (the TR4 cervix key, the TR1 FNAC key, TR14 size as a bar, TR27 dissect-first, TR22 reversed tamoxifen action). Losses: PTEN and STK11 (S2.numbers_q) and the S5.r2 and S6.tt_p1 partials carry no wrong model, so a choice of them tells a teacher nothing. The report (sim/misconceived.report.json) matches its walk for calibration and traps; see r9_reports.

segments.reason: Probe-first hook with trap-mapped options (S1.gate TR4, S1.tissue TR1, S1.vig TR17) and a retest in a new form at S1.re4. Weak: the feedback shape repeats the same 'not right' opener; S1.tissue_partial gives no wrong model.

Strong tempting-then-refute at S2.entry_t10 and S2.vign_t10 (TR10), and S2.brca_t8 (TR8). Flaws: PTEN and STK11 are filler at S2.numbers_q; S2.contrast tells the lobular/ductal contrast after the first probe; S2.family_q partials are two near-identical wrong pairings.

Clinical picture and work-up: S3.nipple (TR20) with a 'frequency versus danger' refutation, S3.skin (TR12), S3.imaging (TR17) with age as the qualifier, S3.tissue (TR1) and S3.staging (TR5). Weak: S3.skin_t3 and S3.tissue_t1 reuse the same generic opener; S3.closing_ok is a second idea on a probe-summary node.

The T, N and M ladder is well built: S4.t_pair vs S4.t_which vs S4.t_vig are three forms of TR12/TR13, and S4.t_n_reveal explains side-of-node for TR2. Flaws: S4.t_which_skin, S4.t_n_neither and S4.t_img_neither name no wrong model; S4.t_pair_a and S4.t_pair_both open with a bare 'That choice is not right.'

Best second explanations in the module: S5.t2_size (a classmate's three-step plan for TR14), S5.t4_nerve (a which-is-wrong probe where the trap statement is true, so it is diagnostic) and S5.t3_why. Flaws: S5.r2_e stacks four rules in one node; S5.r3 key is the only option with a purpose clause; S5.t1_op has no hint or 'Not sure' option; S5.r1_t opens with a bare refusal.

Systemic therapy is taught by menopausal and tissue contrasts (S6.ts_p1, S6.ts_p2, S6.tt_p2), and S6.why_p gives the mechanism for chemotherapy first. Flaws: S6.ls_show2, S6.ts_show2 and S6.tt_show2 repeat their first explanations word for word, so a second visit gets no new explanation; S6.tt_p1 'osteoporosis' partial is filler.

Exam-trap run with a which-is-not drill and tempting lines on most traps (S7.p1_t, S7.p5_t, S7.p11_t). Flaws: fourteen probes in a row with the same 'That choice is not right.' template and little new teaching between them; S7.p9 stem spells out the T4a list ('ribs, intercostal muscles and serratus move freely'), so the key falls out by elimination; S7.p1_t and S7.p3_t sure notes repeat the body.

Consolidation with good discriminators (S8.cut 'relative factor', S8.bone, S8.numb). Flaws: S8.male key 'Klinefelter' is the only non-gene option; S8.tam and S8.axil keys are the only long, rationale-bearing options; S8.axil, S8.numb, S8.tam, S8.labc and S8.male have no hint option; S8.axil_b has only 'Try again'.

best_parts: node S1.gate_t4 and S1.re4_t4: the cervix key named as the lure, then the same trap re-tested in a new form at S1.re4 (TR4)
node S2.entry_t10: 'commonest is not the same as fits the picture' refutes TR10 with the mechanism, not a repeat of the answer
node S5.t2_size: a classmate's three-step plan with one wrong step is a clean second explanation for TR14
node S5.t4_nerve: the trap statement is the true one, so a learner holding the long-thoracic model picks it, which makes the probe diagnostic (TR15)
node S6.why_p: the emboli-in-skin-lymphatics explanation of why drugs come first (TR16)
node S8.tam: a classmate-correction probe with a uterine-risk key and a thrombosis partial separates TR22 from the partial model
flaws: ~80 wrong-option feedback nodes open with the bare line 'That choice is not right.' (examples: S4.t_pair_a, S4.t_which_skin, S5.r1_t, S7.p1_t, S7.p8_t, S8.tis_t); R8 and R4 cost
S2.numbers_pten, S2.numbers_stk: filler partials; the feedback itself says they tempt only as known names, so no learner holding the 13/17 swap would pick them
S8.male_ok: key 'Klinefelter syndrome' is the only non-gene option among three; findable by form
S8.tam: key 'Tamoxifen can raise endometrial cancer risk, so bleeding needs checking' is the only option with a rationale clause; findable by form
S5.r3: key 'Sentinel lymph node biopsy to stage the axilla' is the only option with a purpose clause; findable by form
S7.p9: stem states the T4a list as absent ('ribs, intercostal muscles and serratus anterior move freely'), so the key falls out by elimination
S6.ls_show2, S6.ts_show2, S6.tt_show2, S6.why_show: 'Show me the reasoning' explanations repeat their first versions word for word; no second explanation on a revisit
S8.axil, S8.numb, S8.tam, S8.labc, S8.male, S5.t1_op: probes offer no hint or 'Not sure' option; R5 cost
S4.t_which_skin, S4.t_n_neither, S4.t_img_neither, S5.r2_p: wrong-option feedback names no wrong model or tempting line
S5.r2_e: four rules (multicentric, previous RT or pregnancy or positive margins or inflammatory, relative size, connective tissue disease) in one explanation; split it
S5.r4_ok: three messages on three ideas (nerve, winging, a summary of all treatments); the summary repeats earlier content

misconceived.report.json.verdict: mostly accurate; the walk recovered every trap, and the report says so, though it marks all twelve objectives 'shaky' with none 'secure' or 'gap'
misconceived.report.json.accurate: headline 'mixed' and overconfident calibration match sure_wrong 20; the trap texts for fell_recovered say the old key can return, which matches the walk; 'redo the O-card' pointers are actionable.
misconceived.report.json.inaccurate: next_steps 'gap' text says 'start with the cards for objectives marked gap' although no objective is marked gap; the 'clear' and 'gap' branches are not reconciled with an all-shaky profile.

r9_reports.not_found: sim/novice.report.json, sim/strong.report.json and sim/guesser.report.json are not present under workshop/surgery/carcinoma-breast/sim/ (only misconceived.report.json was readable). R9 for novice, strong and guesser could not be judged; the module R9 score rests on the path and on the one report.

merge_ideas: Use the S5.t2_size classmate-plan format (a plan with one wrong step) as the wrong-option template for the S7 traps, replacing the bare 'That choice is not right.' opener with a named lure.
Give each 'Show me the reasoning' node a second, different explanation on revisit (a worked contrast or a classmate correction), so the S6 and S7 loops do not repeat.
Add the S8.tis-style two-question hint to S8.axil, S8.numb, S8.tam, S8.labc and S8.male, so the consolidation segment has the same hint ladder as S1 to S4.
Put a rationale clause on every option or on none (S8.tam, S8.axil, S5.r3), so the key is not the only long option; keep the S2.entry_t10 mechanism sentence for the trap feedback.
Replace PTEN and STK11 at S2.numbers_q with the wrong BRCA-arm pairing of another trap, so every distractor carries a wrong model.
notes: Module read node by node across all segments S1 to S8, the trap map, claim bank and report.json. Factual accuracy not judged (knowledge-only mode). The module is large (about 330 nodes); the walk was done by reading, not by running validate. Only misconceived.report.json was found among the sim reports.
